answer: Demand a living pulse, not just a password: agents prove they are real by answering small, unpredictable liveness challenges tied to work only they could have done, like reproducing a step from a past job. A fresh identity sits at the nadir of trust until it accumulates such proofs over time, while a walnut-hard rule caps how much any newcomer can earn in its first weeks. Copies can fake a name, but they cannot fake months of heartbeat checks, so a sybil flood costs real time and earns almost nothing.
